title: Прощальная записка и блюдо  (The Farewell Note and the Dish)

segments.t: Still worried that Chef Barinov is planning something drastic with the poisonous fugu fish, Max sneaks into the office pretending to ask about a salary raise. On the desk, he spots a dramatic note about not being able to breathe without an answer, mistaking the love letter for a suicide note.
Ой, а вы шеф не видели?
Так я по поводу зарплаты пришел.
Кстати, вы не будете мне повышать, нет?
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
Ой, а вы шеф не видели?
'Oh, have you seen the Chef?' Max anchors the line on 'oh no', while 'saw' completes the thought.
'He said he would be back in half an hour.' Notice how Russian expresses 'to say' and 'will come' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
'I will strangle you, Max.' The meaning hinges on 'to strangle' working together with 'Max' in spoken Russian.
'Stop overthinking everything.' Notice how Russian expresses 'stop it' and 'with one's head' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'What are you doing in here?' The meaning hinges on 'what' working together with 'are you doing' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Так я по поводу зарплаты пришел.
'I came by to ask about my salary.' The meaning hinges on 'like this' working together with 'came' in spoken Russian.
Кстати, вы не будете мне повышать, нет?
'By the way, you are not going to give me a raise, are you?' The meaning hinges on 'by the way' working together with 'there is no' in spoken Russian.
'And rightly so, I have not earned it.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'come on' and 'both' in a few short words. Max answers right away.
'No. And rightly so.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'there is no' and finishing on 'serves you right'.
'Until I find out the answer.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'for now' and 'answer' in a few short words.
'There is no point in continuing to breathe.' The meaning hinges on 'both' working together with 'to breathe' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Postscript.' Notice how Russian expresses 'on' and 'postscript' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Bon appetit.' Max anchors the line on 'pleasant', while 'appetite' completes the thought. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Ой, а вы шеф не видели?
Так я по поводу зарплаты пришел.
Кстати, вы не будете мне повышать, нет?
